stances_toward.note: Gazprom holds 50% plus one share of Moldovagaz (with Transnistria 13%) and claims a debt of USD 709m, which a 2023 audit commissioned by Chișinău put at USD 8.6m. Moldova said on 2 Oct 2023 that it would stop buying Gazprom gas; Gazprom stopped deliveries on 1 Jan 2025, citing that debt. The grade is 'rival' because friction is institutional (ownership, debt, a contract valid until Oct 2026) and not directed at the firm's destruction; Moldova still depends on Moldovagaz as the legal supply channel to Transnistria. Bond - grievance: the debt dispute and the use of gas as a lever in 2022 and 2025.

relations_to.summary: OMV won an ICC award of EUR 230m against Gazprom Export on 13 Nov 2024 for the stopped German supplies and set it off against its Austrian contract invoices; Gazprom Export cut deliveries on 16 Nov 2024 and OMV terminated the long-term contract on 11 Dec 2024 with immediate effect, citing fundamental breaches. A separate Stockholm (SCC) award of EUR 48m was also set off in December 2024.

relations_to.summary: Fifteen-year contracts signed in Sep 2021 for up to 4.5 bcm a year of Russian gas; Hungary has challenged the EU's ban on Russian gas before the Court of Justice (filed 2 Feb 2026) and no source shows the suit withdrawn.
relations_to.note: Gazprom's release could not be re-fetched on 2026-10-12 (connection refused); the 4.5 bcm ceiling is the figure already held in the HUN card and should be re-checked against the release.

relations_to.summary: Moldova stopped buying gas from Gazprom in late 2023 (energy minister, 2 Oct 2023) and Gazprom halted all supply on 1 Jan 2025 when Ukrainian transit ended, citing Moldovagaz's debt. Chișinău-controlled Moldova now buys European gas; Russian gas reaches Transnistria only through intermediaries.
